reasons.C: Closest in movement and stance: one long paragraph that mixes long semicolon-joined sentences with short blunt ones, a dry ironic aside, a confiding first person and an empty-versus-full antithesis at the close; the exclamation, 'verily' and the personified Silence overdo it a little.
reasons.B: Right period diction, dashes and semicolons, but smoother and more lyrical (restless dog, sparrow, sunlight) than the passage's dry, plain-spoken irony, and split into tidy paragraphs.
reasons.A: Modern plain register with no semicolons or dashes, even short declaratives and a contemporary confessional tone; it doesn't read like a period essayist.
